title: github_deploy_yml docstring overstates SHA propagation (no job output exists)
description: The docstring states 'The impact-analysis job outputs the deployed git SHA so the production workflow can verify it is deploying exactly what was tested.' The generated impact-analysis job has no `outputs:` declaration; its final step only writes `echo "Staged commit: $GITHUB_SHA" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (lines 510-511), a human-readable summary. The separate production workflow obtains the SHA solely from a manual `workflow_dispatch` input the operator types (github_deploy_prod_yml lines 533-540); GitHub Actions cannot read another workflow run's job outputs anyway. So there is no programmatic SHA hand-off as the docstring implies; the operator must manually copy the SHA from the run summary. The code is sensible, but the docstring misdescribes the mechanism and could mislead a maintainer into thinking automatic propagation exists.
evidence: Docstring lines 407-409 vs. job body lines 488-512 (no `outputs:` key; only a STEP_SUMMARY echo) and github_deploy_prod_yml lines 533-540 (sha is a workflow_dispatch input, default blank).
